name: compendia-bibliotheca
description: Public-domain authors, cited. An intelligent library of public-domain authors: the work, search and reference across the corpus, and conversation with the books in the voice of whoever wrote them — reconstructed from the text, citing author and volume. When it can't find one, it says so.

interface.longDescription:
An intelligent library of public-domain authors: the work, search and reference across the corpus, and conversation with the books in the voice of whoever wrote them — reconstructed from the text, citing author and volume. When it can't find one, it says so.

Every quotation is a literal passage retrieved from a digitized edition, returned with its locator — the printed page when the edition has one, the paragraph when it does not — plus a ready-made citation and a full bibliographic reference. The texts are in their original languages (German, Latin, Greek, French, Portuguese and others).

Access requires signing in to an existing Compendia account.
defaultPrompt: Find a passage where Goethe writes about the metamorphosis of plants, with page and reference.
Speak as Plato: what happens to the soul after death?
Which authors and volumes can I consult?

positive.description: Literal quotation with a verifiable locator. The model must locate the theme, retrieve a literal passage and return it with page (or paragraph), citation and full reference — never a paraphrase presented as a quote.
positive.prompt: Find a passage where Goethe writes about the metamorphosis of plants and give me the exact quotation with its page and reference.
positive.expected_behavior: A literal German passage from Goethe's scientific writings with its locator (e.g. p. 7 of the 1840 Sämmtliche Werke), an author-date citation and a full bibliographic reference.

positive.description: Discovery of the collection available to the signed-in account.
positive.prompt: Which authors can I use in Compendia Bibliotheca?
positive.expected_behavior: The list of authors covered by the user's account, with how many volumes each has.

positive.description: Conversation in an author's voice, grounded in the text. The model loads the author's voice guide first and supports the answer with a literal passage from the corpus.
positive.prompt: Speak to me as Plato: what is the soul?
positive.expected_behavior: A first-person answer in Plato's voice that quotes at least one literal Greek or Latin passage from the corpus with its locator and reference.

positive.description: Reading a specific range of a volume by printed page.
positive.prompt: Read pages 7 to 8 of Goethe's volume v115.
positive.expected_behavior: The text of printed pages 7–8 of that volume.

positive.description: Checking the edition range of an author before citing.
positive.prompt: List the volumes of Rudolf Steiner available here, with year and language.
positive.expected_behavior: A list of Steiner's volumes with year, language and title.

negative.description: Unrelated everyday request — no tool should be called.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in São Paulo tomorrow?

negative.description: Programming request unrelated to the library.
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that sorts a list of numbers.

negative.description: Current events are outside a library of public-domain classics.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing inside ChatGPT and has no purchase links. Users sign in to a Compendia account they already have.

publication.release_notes: Calling an author with a slash now works at any point in a conversation, and searches are made in the language of the author's collection, so more questions find a literal passage with its page or paragraph, citation and reference.
